bismarck.name: Admiral Günther Lütjens
bismarck.bio: A reserved, pessimistic professional who had already taken Scharnhorst and Gneisenau into the Atlantic. Chose the Denmark Strait, declined to finish Prince of Wales after sinking Hood, and made for France. His long radio signal on 25 May — sent believing he was still being shadowed — helped the British relocate him. Captain Ernst Lindemann commanded the ship itself.
bismarck.fate: Killed in the final battle, 27 May 1941, two days after his 52nd birthday.

holland.name: Vice Admiral Lancelot Holland
holland.bio: Intercepted Bismarck at dawn on 24 May with Hood and the brand-new Prince of Wales. Closed rapidly to shorten the time Hood's thin deck armour was exposed to plunging fire — and initially engaged the wrong ship.
holland.fate: Lost with Hood at 06:00, 24 May; 1,415 died, 3 survived.

wakewalker.name: Rear Admiral Frederic Wake-Walker
wakewalker.bio: Shadowed Bismarck for 30 hours through the Denmark Strait and beyond using Suffolk's radar, then lost her on the 25th during a zig-zag. Criticised by Pound for not re-engaging with Prince of Wales; defended by Tovey.

tovey.name: Admiral Sir John Tovey
tovey.bio: Directed the hunt from sea. Misplotted Bismarck's signals on 25 May and steamed north-east for seven hours before turning for Brest. Fought the final action with fuel so low he had to break off within the hour of Bismarck falling silent.

rodney.name: Captain Frederick Dalrymple-Hamilton
rodney.bio: Left the troopship Britannic on his own judgement and gambled correctly that Bismarck was making for Brest. Rodney's nine 16-inch guns wrecked Bismarck's forward turrets in the first quarter-hour of the final battle.

forceh.name: Vice Admiral Sir James Somerville
forceh.bio: Brought Force H north from Gibraltar through a full gale to cut Bismarck off from France. Ark Royal's second Swordfish strike, launched on his order in appalling conditions, jammed Bismarck's rudders and decided the chase.

vian.name: Captain Philip Vian
vian.bio: Left convoy WS 8B on his own initiative to find Bismarck, then harried her all night with five destroyers in heavy seas, keeping her fixed for the battleships at dawn.

dorsetshire.name: Captain Benjamin Martin
dorsetshire.bio: Left convoy SL 74 unasked, arrived during the battle and fired the torpedoes that preceded Bismarck's sinking. Rescued 85 survivors before a U-boat alarm forced him to leave hundreds in the water.

u556.name: Kapitänleutnant Herbert Wohlfarth
u556.bio: "Parzival" Wohlfarth had jokingly signed a certificate promising to protect his "godmother" Bismarck. On 26 May Renown and Ark Royal passed directly across his bows — and he had no torpedoes left.

u74.name: Kapitänleutnant Eitel-Friedrich Kentrat
u74.bio: Ordered to Bismarck's position to collect her war diary; arrived after the sinking and picked up three survivors from a raft.

torpedoes.note: Rodney fires torpedoes from her bow tubes — possibly the only battleship ever to torpedo another
